question:
**Computer Graphics/3D Modeling Case Study**

A triangular 3D mesh is defined by points U(2, -1, 3), V(7, 3, 4), and W(1, 5, 6). The normal to the face determines lighting and shading in rendering.

(a) Calculate the vector area of triangle UVW using vector cross product.

(b) Find the unit normal vector to the face, ensuring consistent orientation (right-hand rule for UVxUW).

(c) If a light arrives from direction $-\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$, what is the cosine of the angle between the face normal and the light direction? Interpret physically.
explanation:
(a)

$\vec{UV} = (7-2)\hat{i} + (3+1)\hat{j} + (4-3)\hat{k} = 5\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 1\hat{k}$

$\vec{UW} = (1-2)\hat{i} + (5+1)\hat{j} + (6-3)\hat{k} = -1\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$

Area of $\triangle UVW = \frac{1}{2}|\vec{UV} \times \vec{UW}|$

Calculate cross product:

$\vec{UV} \times \vec{UW} = \left|\begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 5 & 4 & 1 \\ -1 & 6 & 3\end{matrix}\right|$

$= \hat{i}(4\times3 - 1\times6) -\hat{j}(5\times3 - 1\times(-1)) + \hat{k}(5\times6 - 4\times(-1))$

$= \hat{i}(12-6) - \hat{j}(15+1) + \hat{k}(30+4)$

$= 6\hat{i} -16\hat{j} +34\hat{k}$

Magnitude $= \sqrt{6^2 + 16^2 + 34^2} = \sqrt{36+256+1156}=\sqrt{1448}$

Area $= \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{1448} = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{1448}}{2}~units^2}$

(b)

Unit normal:

$\hat{n} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1448}} (6\hat{i} - 16\hat{j} + 34\hat{k})$

(c)

Light vector: $\vec{L} = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$

Unit vector $\vec{l} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}(-1\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}) = -\frac{1}{3}\hat{i} - \frac{2}{3}\hat{j} - \frac{2}{3}\hat{k}$

The cosine of the angle is $\hat{n} \cdot \vec{l}$:

$= \frac{1}{\sqrt{1448}}[6*(-1/3) + (-16)*(-2/3) + 34*(-2/3)]$

$= \frac{1}{\sqrt{1448}}[ -2 + 32/3 - 68/3 ]$

$= \frac{1}{\sqrt{1448}}[ -2 + (32-68)/3 ]$

$= \frac{1}{\sqrt{1448}}[ -2 -12 ] = \frac{-14}{\sqrt{1448}}$

Physical interpretation: Negative value means light is on the opposite side of the surface (normal and light direction more than 90°).

options.A:
(a) Vector area magnitude $=\frac{\sqrt{1448}}{2}$ units²
(b) Unit normal $=\frac{6\hat{i}-16\hat{j}+34\hat{k}}{\sqrt{1448}}$
(c) $\cos\theta=\frac{-14}{\sqrt{1448}}$, so light is on the opposite side.
options.B:
(a) Vector area magnitude $=\sqrt{1448}$ units²
(b) Unit normal $=\frac{6\hat{i}-16\hat{j}+34\hat{k}}{\sqrt{1448}}$
(c) $\cos\theta=\frac{14}{\sqrt{1448}}$, so light is on the same side.
options.C:
(a) Vector area magnitude $=\frac{\sqrt{724}}{2}$ units²
(b) Unit normal $=\frac{6\hat{i}+16\hat{j}+34\hat{k}}{\sqrt{1448}}$
(c) $\cos\theta=\frac{-14}{\sqrt{724}}$, so light is on the opposite side.
options.D:
(a) Vector area magnitude $=\frac{\sqrt{1448}}{2}$ units²
(b) Unit normal $=\frac{5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{42}}$
(c) $\cos\theta=0$, so light is perpendicular to the surface.
